Background (from the session that started this one):
Paper Ghosts is the owner's DEV / Hacktoberfest Week 4 entry, in the private repo `Hotragn/Paperghosts` (this folder). You type a US town and read the real ghost reports its newspapers printed from 1774 to 1963, taken from the AmericanStories dataset and the Library of Congress scans. Every claim is backed by a quote that code has verified. The spec is `Docs/BRIEF.md`, which is the owner's and wins any conflict. The look is `Docs/UI-IDEAS.md`. I'm the engineering manager in another session: I send one small step at a time and review it before sending the next. The phases and gates are in `Docs/BUILD-PLAN.md`, which arrives in step 1.1. Rules: never print, log or echo secrets from `.env`, and check keys by shape only. No global installs and no Homebrew. Stop and ask before anything public (repo visibility, deploys, DNS, posting) or any spending beyond free tiers and existing credits. Make small commits on phase branches and open pull requests into `main`; I merge them. Record numbered decisions in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, and end each milestone with a STATUS block in `Docs/RESUME.md`. Entire capture is enabled through `.claude/settings.json`; don't touch it. Superpowers and Ponytail are enabled. Use Superpowers' process skills where they fit, and Ponytail for minimal code, but the deliverables in `BUILD-PLAN.md` are required scope. Don't run brainstorming Q&A with the owner; put questions in your reply to me. Start every reply to me with `<step>: DONE` or `<step>: BLOCKED — reason`, then 150 words at most.

=== DECISIONS.md
# Decisions

Numbered, each with its reason. Newest at the bottom.

## Before Step 1 (2026-10-29)

**1. The source is AmericanStories, not the Chronicling America API.**
The old Chronicling America JSON API returns 404. AmericanStories has the same scans as structured article text, under CC-BY-4.0. It also keeps each article's bounding box, which lets the site crop the original clipping from the Library of Congress image service.

**2. Read the whole archive (180 year files), not a sample.**
A full pass is 340 GB. At the measured 66 MB/s that is about 1.5 h of transfer, which is affordable. Full coverage makes the counts honest and lets every US town get its results.

**3. Stream every file and never keep the tarballs.**
The disk has 37 GB free, and the largest year alone is 7.6 GB.

**4. Walks is an optional layer on top of search, and it is built last.**
Halloween and Día de los Muertos are nights when people go out, both to haunted places and to graves. On Oct 29, none of 598 posts offered walks built from original sources. The nearest were GeoLetter (letters left at places) and Trailhead (general outing cards).
Walks also gives two tools a real job:
- SerpApi's Google Maps results answer "is it still standing?"
- Atlas geo queries answer "near me".

Old reports are often vague, and many of the places are gone. So walks use only precisely located public stops, every pin shows how precise it is, and Walks is cut if Steps 1–4 run late.

**5. One main tool (Tinker); the others support it. MongoDB Atlas, not Tiger Data. No .tech domain.**
Week 2's partner winners each made one partner the core of the product and proved it under failure. Our Week 2 entry, Cubby, spread thin uses across seven partners and won nothing. So the depth goes into the Tinker reader, and Atlas, Temporal, Render and Sentry each get one real job.

Why Atlas over Tiger Data:
- Atlas is already set up; Tiger Data would need a new account.
- Articles are JSON documents, and Atlas covers all three searches we need (geo, fuzzy text, vectors) in one place.
- On Oct 29, three entries claimed Tiger Data, including Still Here by the author who won Tiger Data in Week 1.

The owner chose not to use a .tech domain.

=== DECISIONS-append.md

## Planning (2026-10-29)

**6. The build runs in five phases with gates, managed by an EM session.**
`BUILD-PLAN.md` maps the `BRIEF.md` steps onto five phases: scaffolding; database, schemas and data models; backend and APIs; frontend; polish and QA. Each milestone ends at a gate the EM checks before the next one starts. The owner manages the schedule, so whether Walks is built is the owner's call at the Phase 4 gate.

**7. Static-first site: the core path is prebuilt JSON, and the live API handles search, near me and similar.**
Free Render web services sleep after a short idle. A judge's first click has to be instant, and an outage at the API, at Atlas or at LoC shouldn't blank the front page, a town or a case.

**8. Stories and printings are counted separately.**
Syndicated ghost stories were reprinted in many papers. Counting each printing as its own ghost would inflate the numbers and duplicate cases. Reprints of a gold article in the training data would also inflate the reader's scores.

**9. Models are selected on a dev split, and the gold set is used only for final evals.**
That keeps the held-out numbers honest.

**10. The investigator's default model is Gemma 4 26B-A4B (QAT), running locally through Ollama. Ultramarine is the comparison run.**
The model is already on this machine (15 GB), it's open-weight, and it keeps the investigation offline. Both runs work the same cases, so the comparison is fair.

**11. The Halloween look comes from the reading room after dark.**
`UI-IDEAS.md` sets the direction: the lamp, the lights off, and the scans as the only imagery. Costume-shop iconography is out.

**12. Config accepts both names for the Ultramarine key.**
`.env` names it `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY`, while `BRIEF.md` says `ULTRAMARINE_API_KEY`. The owner's file stays as it is.

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness
Copying and appending are done. Next I'll create the `phase-1-scaffold` branch, stage only the requested paths, check that no secrets are staged, and commit.

1	# Product brief: Paper Ghosts
2	
3	A newspaper's archive of old clippings is called its morgue. Paper Ghosts is a morgue for every ghost that America's newspapers reported between 1774 and 1963.
4	
5	## What it is
6	You type a town and get the real ghost reports printed in or about that town. They come straight from old newspapers, not from legends retold on the web. Each report shows:
7	- **the original clipping**, cropped from the Library of Congress page scan, next to its transcription
8	- the paper, date and place, plus who saw what and where
9	- **what happened next**: follow-up stories, the debunking, the arrest of the prankster, the family that moved out
10	- **the person behind the ghost**, when a name leads to a real death notice or inquest in the same papers
11	- **then and now**: what the 1890s paper said, next to what today's web and ghost tours say about the same place
12	
13	The site never writes a ghost story. Everything it shows was printed in a newspaper, and every claim links to the clipping it came from.
14	
15	**Walks: an optional layer, built only after the core works.** Search stays the front door. On top of it:
16	- **Near me:** a map of reports around you. Your location is rounded to about 1 km, used for that one query and never logged.
17	- **Self-guided walks:** offered only where a town has at least 3 precisely located stops that the public can see from a street, all within about 3 km.
18	  - Each stop shows its clipping, what happened next, and what stands there now.
19	  - A walk can be saved as a printable page, so it works offline.
20	- **Road trips** across several towns: a stretch goal, and the first thing to cut.
21	
22	## Who it's for
23	Anyone curious about their own town on Halloween, plus local historians, genealogists and ghost-tour guides who want the original source rather than the retelling.
24	
25	## Non-negotiables
26	1. **Secrets:**
27	   - Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log, echo or commit them; read them through the environment only.
28	   - `.env` is already at the repo root, and `.gitignore` covers it. It holds `TINKER_API_KEY`, `MONGODB_URI` and `RENDER_API_KEY`, plus a few unused keys.
29	   - For Sentry it holds `SENTRY_DSN` (API project), `SENTRY_DSN_WEB` (web project), and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` with `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT`. The token can read events and traces, and write projects.

59	## Data (verified 2026-10-29)
60	**AmericanStories** (Hugging Face `dell-research-harvard/AmericanStories`, CC-BY-4.0, from Harvard's Dell Research): article-level text extracted from the Library of Congress's Chronicling America scans.
61	- **Files:** 180 per-year files, `faro_{year}.tar.gz`, 340 GB in total.
62	  - Download: `https://huggingface.co/datasets/dell-research-harvard/AmericanStories/resolve/main/faro_{year}.tar.gz`
63	  - Sizes: 1850 is 0.99 GB; 1897–1920 are 6–7.6 GB each.

65	  - `lccn`: `{title, state, lccn, …}`, where `title` includes the place of publication, e.g. "The New York herald. [volume] (New York [N.Y.]) 1840-1920"
66	  - `edition`: `{date}`
67	  - `scan`: `{width, height, raw_data_loc}`
68	  - `full articles`: a list of `{headline, article, byline, bbox, bbox_list, id, full_article_id}`
69	- **Machine limits:**
70	  - Download speed measured 66 MB/s, so a full pass is about 1.5 h of transfer.
71	  - Only **37 GB of disk is free**. Stream every file and never store the tarballs.

74	**Page scans for the clippings** (public domain, Library of Congress IIIF image service):
75	- `raw_data_loc` looks like `https://chroniclingamerica.loc.gov/data/batches/{batch}/data/{lccn}/{reel}/{issue}/{seq}.jp2`.
76	- The crop is `https://tile.loc.gov/image-services/iiif/service:ndnp:{awardee}:batch_{batch}:data:{lccn}:{reel}:{issue}:{seq}/{x},{y},{w},{h}/pct:50/0/default.jpg`, where:
77	  - `awardee` is the first part of the batch name (`dlc_marcus_ver01` gives `dlc`)
78	  - `bbox` is `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` in scan pixels, so `w = x2-x1` and `h = y2-y1`
79	- This was verified on one 1850 New York Herald article, and the crop matched the text. Verify it across many batches before relying on it.
80	- Use `bbox_list` for articles that run across columns.

82	**Gone:** the old Chronicling America JSON API returns 404, so the dataset above is the source.

Data flow, step by step 80 81 ### 3.1 Ingest (`IngestArchiveWorkflow`) 82 - **Input:** a list of years, all 180 by default. 83 - **Output per year, under `data/`:** 84 - `candidates/{year}.jsonl.zst`: articles that hit the lexicon, with the matched terms, page metadata and scan location 85 - `counts/{year}.json`: pages, articles and candidates, broken down by state and by term 86 - `samples/{year}.jsonl.zst`: a reservoir sample of non-candidates, plus a near-miss pool (articles with words like "knocking", "strange noises" or "spirits" but no ghost term). Both feed the recall measurement. 87 - `manifests/{year}.json`: source URL, bytes read, lexicon version, code version, start and finish times 88 - **One activity per year file:** stream, gunzip, and read tar members one at a time. The tarball never touches the disk. 89 - Heartbeats carry progress (members done, bytes read). 90 - Retry policy: exponential backoff with a bounded number of attempts. 91 - **Idempotent:** 92 - Outputs are written to a temporary file and renamed when complete. 93 - A year whose manifest matches the current lexicon and code versions is skipped. 94 - A killed worker re-runs only unfinished years. The year in flight restarts from its beginning, because a gzip stream can't seek. The kill-test write-up says so. 95 - **Concurrency:** bounded, starting from what Phase 1 measures for download speed and parse speed on this machine (10 cores). 96 - **Disk:** about 35 GB is free, so all ingest outputs together must stay under 10 GB, measured and reported. 97 98 ### 3.2 Gold set and reader 99 - **Gold set:** 100 - 150–300 candidates, stratified by decade and lexicon term and including near-miss items. 101 - Frozen before any training: the split and its hash are committed under `eval/gold/`. 102 - The build agent labels it before seeing any model output, from the OCR text and the scan crop where the OCR is unclear. 103 - The labelling rules for hard cases (séance reports, reprinted fiction, hoax exposures, humour columns) are written in `eval/gold/POLICY.md` before labelling starts. 104 - **Training data:** the teacher labels a separate pool. No gold article, and no reprint of a gold article, may appear in it. 105 - **Model selection** happens on a dev split. The gold set is touched only for final evaluations. 106 - **Full pass:** the tuned student reads every triaged candidate and writes `data/reader/{year}.jsonl.zst`. Every field either passes the quote verifier or becomes "not stated". 107 108 ### 3.3 Geocode, cluster, embed, load 109 - Places are resolved against GeoNames. Every location records its precision (town, street or building) and its source. Street or building coordinates exist only when a source supplies them. 110 - Printings of the same story are grouped. Counts on the site say which they count: stories or printings. 111 - Stories get one embedding each, from the earliest legible printing. 112 - The loader upserts by stable IDs, so re-running it is safe. 113 114 ### 3.4 Follow-up harvest 115 - The top 30–60 cases are picked by a written, versioned rule: a verified place, named people or a specific place, and a legible clipping. 116 - The years those cases need are grouped, and each year file is streamed once. 117 - From each stream, the harvest pulls articles that match a case's named people, its specific place, or its town within a date window. 118 - Output goes to `data/harvest/{case_id}.jsonl`. 119 120 ### 3.5 Investigator (the main Temporal story) 121 - `InvestigateCaseWorkflow(case_id, model)` runs a loop: plan, call tools, read, write claims, verify. 122 - Every model call and every tool call is an activity, with an idempotency key made from the workflow ID and the step number. 123 - Temporal records each result in the workflow history. After a crash the workflow replays and reuses those results, so no completed model call or web search is repeated. 124 - A call that is in flight when the worker dies has no recorded result, so Temporal retries it. The idempotency key lets a provider that supports one drop the duplicate, and the kill test counts these retries rather than claiming there are none. 125 - **Tools:** 126 - `search_archive` over the harvested and candidate articles, using a local full-text index and Atlas Search 127 - `get_article` 128 - `find_death_notices(name, place, window)` 129 - `web_search` through SerpApi, with a budget counter that persists across runs 130 - `wikipedia` for the "now" side when the SerpApi budget runs out (the card says so) 131 - **Guardrails in code, not just in the prompt:** 132 - A claim is kept only if it cites at least one clipping and its quote verifies against that clipping. Dropped claims are logged with the reason. 133 - A cause of death is stated only as printed. 134 - The link between a ghost and a death is graded strong, possible or weak, with its reasons listed (name match, place match, date gap). 135 - **Output:** a `cases` document, plus one Sentry trace per case with a span per step carrying model, tokens, cost and latency. 136 - **Budgets:** a maximum number of steps per case, a maximum number of web searches per case, and a global SerpApi counter (the free plan is 250 searches a month). 137 138 ```mermaid 139 sequenceDiagram 140 participant W as InvestigateCase workflow 141 participant M as Model activity 142 participant T as Tool activities 143 W->>M: step 1, plan (result recorded) 144 W->>T: step 2, search_archive and find_death_notices (recorded) 145 Note over W: worker killed here 146 W-->>W: replay from history: steps 1 and 2 reuse recorded results 147 W->>M: step 3, write claims 148 W->>T: step 4, verify quotes and save the case file 149 ``` 150 151 ### 3.6 Static export and the site 152 - `export_static` reads Atlas and writes: 153 - `front.json`: printed-on-this-night candidates, ticker headlines and totals 154 - `towns/index.json`: a compact town index for search on the device 155 - `towns/{place_id}.json` and `cases/{report_id}.json` 156 - `reel.json`: the archive chart 157 - The API contract is in `SRS.md` section 6. 158 - Both services are defined in `render.yaml`. CI needs no secrets; tests that need the network are marked and skipped there. 239 - **CD (Render):** a Blueprint with an API web service and a static site. It auto-deploys from `main` only after the owner approves the first deploy. 240 - Render environment variables are set by the owner. 241 - Atlas network access must allow Render's servers; that change also needs the owner's yes. 242 - **Releases:** Sentry releases are tagged with the git SHA. 243 244 ## 7. Security and privacy 245 - **Secrets:** 246 - Secrets reach code only through environment variables. 247 - `config.py` redacts them in `repr`, logs and errors. 248 - The Ultramarine key is named `PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY` in `.env`; config also accepts `ULTRAMARINE_API_KEY`. 249 - **Sentry:** `send_default_pii=False`, and a `before_send` hook strips coordinates and query strings. 250 - **Near me:** coordinates are rounded to about 1 km on the device and again on the server, used for that one query, and never logged. 251 - **Secret scanning:** a scanner runs in CI. 252 - Entire is on with telemetry off, and its checkpoints sync to the private `origin`. 253 - Before the repo goes public, the Entire checkpoint refs and the recorded sessions are scanned for secrets. 254 - **The people in the archive:** nobody is named except as the papers printed them, and nothing about how they died is guessed. 255 256 ## 8. Architecture risks and what answers them 257 258 | Risk | Answer | 259 |---|---| 260 | Ingest is limited by CPU, not network | Measure parse speed in Phase 1 and set concurrency from it | 261 | Too many candidates for the reader budget | A triage stage measured for recall, plus cost per 10,000 articles and a Tinker credit check before the full pass | 262 | Reprints inflate counts and leak gold into training | Reprint clustering, counts labelled as stories or printings, and a leakage check script | 263 | Rough OCR | Fuzzy quote verification, and optionally Gemma re-reading the scan image when the OCR is unreadable | 264 | LoC image service is slow or down | Lazy loading, cached crops for the top content, and a text fallback | 265 | Render free services sleep | The core path is served from static JSON | 266 | Atlas free tier is 512 MB | Only stories go to Atlas; the bulk stays local and the article says so | 267 | Gemma 4 26B on 24 GB of RAM | Never run it alongside the local student; measure tokens per second in Phase 1 | 268

1	# SRS: Paper Ghosts
2	
3	Software requirements, each with an ID and how it is verified. The gates in `BUILD-PLAN.md` check against these IDs. The product view is in `PRD.md`, and the design is in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
4	
5	## 1. Definitions
6	- **Article:** one article region from AmericanStories, with its text, headline, bounding boxes and page.
7	- **Printing:** one article as printed in one paper on one date.
8	- **Story:** a cluster of printings of the same text. Syndicated stories were reprinted in many papers.
9	- **Candidate:** an article that hit the lexicon.
10	- **Report:** a candidate the reader classified as `kind = report`.
11	- **Case:** a report the investigator worked on.
12	- **Clipping:** the crop of the page scan for one article.
13	- **Verified quote:** a quote the verifier found in the source text, within the calibrated fuzzy threshold.
14	- **Precision:** how exactly a location is known: town, street or building.

1	# Build plan
2	
3	How the build runs: five phases, each split into milestones, each milestone with a persona, deliverables and an exit gate. An engineering manager (EM) session writes the prompt for each milestone, a build session carries it out, and the EM checks the result before the next milestone starts.
4	
5	## 1. How each milestone runs
6	1. **The EM sends the milestone prompt:** its scope, its deliverables, and the gate it must pass.
7	2. **The build session works on a branch** named `phase-<n>-<slug>`.
8	   - Small commits, pushed to the private repo, with a pull request into `main`.
9	   - It ends with a STATUS block in `RESUME.md`.
10	   - Its final message starts with one line: `<milestone>: GATE PASSED` or `<milestone>: BLOCKED — <reason>`.
11	3. **The EM reviews:**
12	   - reads the diff, and re-runs the gate commands
13	   - spot-checks outputs against their sources, using a random sample
14	   - checks the non-negotiables: no secrets, no invented numbers, verified quotes, respect for the dead
15	   - checks that CI is green
16	4. **Pass:** the EM merges the pull request and sends the next prompt. **Fail:** the EM sends a numbered fix list, and the gate runs again.
17	5. **Owner gates** always stop and ask first: making the repo public, deploying, DNS, posting anywhere, and spending money.

34	- A Makefile. Targets that belong to later phases exist as stubs that say which phase builds them.

39	  - Atlas: tier, version, storage limit and storage used, and whether Atlas Search and Vector Search indexes can be created (create one of each on a scratch collection, then drop it)

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

1	# Writing Good Tests
2	
3	**Load this reference when:** writing or changing tests, adding mocks, or
4	adding cleanup/helper methods for tests.
5	
6	## Overview
7	
8	A test exists to catch a specific break. Two principles govern everything
9	here:
10	
11	```
12	1. Every test names the break it catches
13	2. Every test exercises the real thing
14	```
15	
16	Strict TDD produces both naturally: a test written first and watched
17	failing against real code has already proven it can fail, and only earns
18	a mock when the real dependency proves slow or external.
19	
20	## Principle 1: Name the Break
21	
22	Before writing the test body, answer: **what production change should
23	make this test fail — and is that change a bug or a decision?** A test
24	earns its place by catching a wrong branch, missing side effect, wrong
25	argument, boundary case, or broken contract.
26	
27	**Derive expectations independently.** Use literals and hand-checked
28	fixtures; table-driven tests with literal `want` values are the preferred
29	shape. An expectation computed by the code under test — or its helpers —
30	passes no matter what that code does:
31	
32	```typescript
33	// ❌ Mirror assertion: the same builder computes both sides — always true
34	const expected = buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' });
35	expect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe(expected);
36	
37	// ✅ Hand-derived literal
38	expect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe('tag:"urgent"');
39	```
40	
41	**No change detectors.** If only intentional decisions can fail a test —
42	a constant's value, exact message wording, private structure — it fires
43	on redesign and sleeps through bugs. Test the behavior that depends on
44	the decision: not `expect(MAX_RETRIES).toBe(5)` but "a failing call is
45	retried 5 times and the 6th attempt never happens."
46	
47	**Behavior, not text.** Asserting that a script, skill, or config
48	contains an exact line proves only that the source is the source. Run
49	scripts against controlled inputs and assert outputs, side effects, or
50	exit codes. Documents that instruct agents are tested by the consuming
51	agent's behavior (superpowers:writing-skills); prose for humans earns no
52	test at all.
53	
54	**Your code, not the framework.** Test the contract your code makes at
55	its boundaries — the route you register, the query you emit, the payload
56	you produce. Upstream mechanics are their maintainers' tests to write
57	(the classic: asserting your router invokes a registered handler — that
58	is the framework's test, not yours). When upstream behavior genuinely
59	surprised you, write one narrow characterization test naming the
60	assumption. The same boundary applies inside your code: constructors,
61	getters, constants, and trivial forwarding earn tests only when they
62	validate, normalize, default, derive, enforce, or cause side effects —
63	otherwise assert the first consumer-visible result that depends on them.
64	
65	### Gate Function
66	
67	```
68	BEFORE writing the test body:
69	  Name the production change that would make this test fail.
70	
71	  Cannot name one            → redesign around an observable behavior
72	  "The source text changed"  → run the artifact and assert its effects
73	  Only intentional decisions → change detector; test the behavior
74	                               that depends on the decision
75	
76	  Confirm the expected value is derived without the code under test.
77	  IF it reuses the code's logic or helpers:
78	    Replace it with a literal or hand-checked fixture
79	```
80	
81	## Principle 2: Exercise the Real Thing
82	
83	**The mock earns no assertions.** A mock assertion passes when the mock
84	is present and fails when it is absent — it says nothing about the
85	component. Assert the real component's behavior; if the mock is what you
86	are checking, unmock it or delete the assertion.
87	
88	```typescript
89	// ✅ Real behavior
90	expect(screen.getByRole('navigation')).toBeInTheDocument();
91	
92	// ❌ Mock existence
93	expect(screen.getByTestId('sidebar-mock')).toBeInTheDocument();
94	```
95	
96	**your human partner's correction:** "Are we testing the behavior of a
97	mock?"
98	
99	**Mock at the right level.** Learn every side effect of the real method
100	before replacing it; mock the slow or external operation and keep what
101	the test depends on real. When unsure, run the test against the real
102	implementation first and observe what actually needs to happen.
103	
104	```typescript
105	// ❌ The mock swallows the config write that duplicate detection reads
106	vi.mock('ToolCatalog', () => ({
107	  discoverAndCacheTools: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined)
108	}));
109	
110	// ✅ Mock only the slow server startup; the config write stays real
111	vi.mock('MCPServerManager');
112	```
113	
114	**Make doubles specific.** When arguments, call counts, or ordering are
115	part of the contract, assert them — a fake that accepts anything verifies
116	nothing. Give each branch (success, error, malformed) its own fixture or
117	spy, so the wrong branch cannot satisfy the expectation.
118	
119	**Mirror real data completely.** Mock the complete structure as it exists
120	in reality — all documented fields — not just the ones your test reads.
121	Partial mocks fail silently when downstream code reads an omitted field:
122	the test passes while integration breaks.
123	
124	**Production classes carry production methods only.** Cleanup that only
125	tests need lives in test utilities, never as a `destroy()` on the
126	production class. Ask: is this method called only from tests? Does this
127	class own this resource's lifecycle? Wrong answers → test utility.
128	
129	**Prefer real components over complex mocks.** When mock setup outgrows
130	the test logic, mocks miss methods the real components have, or tests
131	break when the mock changes, switch to an integration test with real
132	components. **your human partner's question:** "Do we need to be using a
133	mock here?"
134	
135	### Gate Function
136	
137	```
138	BEFORE adding a mock or test helper:
139	  List the real method's side effects; keep the ones the test
140	  depends on real — mock the slow/external level below them.
141	
142	  Mock responses mirror the complete real structure.
143	
144	  A method only tests call lives in test utilities, not production.
145	
146	  About to assert on the mock itself?
147	    Unmock it or delete the assertion.
148	```
149	
150	## Tests Ship With the Implementation
151	
152	The TDD cycle — failing test, minimal implementation, refactor — is what
153	"complete" means. Ship the tests the behavior needs and only those:
154	trivial code and human prose earn none, and a test written to satisfy
155	process costs maintenance forever.
156	
157	## The Mutation Check
158	
159	Before finishing, mentally mutate the production code; at least one test
160	should fail for each realistic mutation:
161	
162	- Wrong constant or argument
163	- Wrong branch handler
164	- Missing state change or side effect
165	- Empty or default return
166	- Missing validation for zero, empty, nil, unauthorized, or malformed input
167	
168	A mutation nothing catches marks the behavior as unprotected — or the
169	test as tautological.
170	
171	## Quick Reference
172	
173	| When you... | Do |
174	|-------------|-----|
175	| Write any test | Name the break it catches — a bug, not a decision |
176	| Build an expected value | Derive it by hand; never with the code under test |
177	| Test a script or document | Run it / pressure-test its consumer; never grep its text |
178	| Reach for a dependency test | Test your boundary contract, not their documented mechanics |
179	| Want to assert on a mocked element | Test the real component, or unmock it |
180	| Are about to mock a method | Learn its side effects; mock the slow/external level |
181	| Build a mock response | Mirror the real structure completely |
182	| Need cleanup only tests use | Put it in test utilities |
183	| Watch mock setup balloon | Switch to an integration test with real components |
184	| Finish a test file | Run the mutation check |
185	
186	## Warning Signs
187	
188	- Setup and assertion share the same object, guaranteeing equality
189	- The test can fail only through a panic, crash, or missing selector
190	- The test fails on every intentional change, never on accidental breakage
191	- Expected values are hidden behind loops, builders, or helpers
192	- The test greps source text, or asserts a removed symbol stays removed
193	- The test would still matter if only the framework remained
194	- The test exists for coverage, checking no side effect or outcome
195	- An assertion checks a `*-mock` test ID, or fails if you remove the mock
196	- A method is called only from test files
197	- Mock setup is more than half the test, or you can't explain why the mock is needed
198	- Mocking "just to be safe"

"""Secrets, private notes and bulk data must never reach git; manifests must."""

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("path", "ignored"),
    [
        (".env", True),
        (".env.local", True),
        ("web/.env.local", True),
        ("Docs/IDEAS.md", True),
        ("data/candidates/1850.jsonl.zst", True),
        ("data/samples/1850.jsonl.zst", True),
        ("data/temporal/temporal.db", True),
        (".env.example", False),
        ("data/manifests/1850.json", False),
    ],
)
def test_private_files_stay_out_of_git(path, ignored):
    # check-ignore treats a tracked file as not ignored, so a force-added .env fails here too
    result = subprocess.run(["git", "check-ignore", "-q", path], cwd=ROOT)
    assert result.returncode in (0, 1), f"git check-ignore errored on {path}"
    assert (result.returncode == 0) == ignored

# Paper Ghosts

Type a US town and read the ghost reports its newspapers printed between 1774 and 1963. The reports come from the AmericanStories dataset and the Library of Congress page scans. The site never writes a ghost story: every claim links to the clipping it came from.

This is a work in progress. The plan is in [`Docs/BUILD-PLAN.md`](Docs/BUILD-PLAN.md), and where the build stands is in [`Docs/RESUME.md`](Docs/RESUME.md).

## Run it

You need `uv`, Node and `pnpm`. Keys go in `.env`, which git ignores.

```bash
make setup   # the Python 3.12 environment and the web shell's packages
make lint    # ruff, oxlint and the TypeScript check
make test    # pytest
make web     # the web shell at http://localhost:5173
```

The other targets print the phase that builds them.

## What it can't do

Filled in as limits are found.

## Failure log

Filled in as failures are found.

## Credits

- Article text: AmericanStories, from Harvard's Dell Research (CC-BY-4.0)
- Page scans: Library of Congress, Chronicling America (public domain)

# Prints only line kinds, names, lengths and yes/no shape facts. Never a character of a value.
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

HEX = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]+")
SLUG = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*")


def facts(name, v):
    out = []
    try:
        if name == "TINKER_API_KEY":
            out.append(f"tml-prefix={v.startswith('tml-')}")
        elif name == "RENDER_API_KEY":
            out.append(f"rnd_prefix={v.startswith('rnd_')}")
        elif name == "SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN":
            out += [f"user-token-prefix={v.startswith('sntryu_')}", f"org-token-prefix={v.startswith('sntrys_')}",
                    f"hex64={bool(HEX.fullmatch(v)) and len(v) == 64}"]
        elif name == "SERPAPI_API_KEY":
            out.append(f"hex64={bool(HEX.fullmatch(v)) and len(v) == 64}")
        elif name == "HF_TOKEN":
            out.append(f"hf_prefix={v.startswith('hf_')}")
        elif name == "MONGODB_URI":
            u = urlsplit(v)
            out += [f"srv={v.startswith('mongodb+srv://')}", f"plain={v.startswith('mongodb://')}",
                    f"user={bool(u.username)}", f"password={bool(u.password)}", f"query={bool(u.query)}",
                    f"path_db={bool(u.path.strip('/'))}"]
        elif name.startswith("SENTRY_DSN"):
            u = urlsplit(v)
            host = u.hostname or ""
            out += [f"https={u.scheme == 'https'}", f"user_hex32={bool(u.username and HEX.fullmatch(u.username) and len(u.username) == 32)}",
                    f"sentry_host={host.endswith('.sentry.io')}", f"us={'.us.sentry.io' in host}", f"de={'.de.sentry.io' in host}",
                    f"path_digits={u.path.strip('/').isdigit()}"]
        elif name in ("SENTRY_ORG", "SENTRY_PROJECT"):
            out.append(f"slug={bool(SLUG.fullmatch(v))}")
        elif name == "ULTRAMARINE_BASE_URL":
            u = urlsplit(v)
            out += [f"https={u.scheme == 'https'}", f"path_v1={u.path.rstrip('/').endswith('/v1')}",
                    f"host_paperinstruments={'paperinstruments' in (u.hostname or '')}"]
        elif name in ("PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY", "ULTRAMARINE_API_KEY", "ULTRAMARINE_MODEL",
                      "GEMINI_API_KEY", "ELEVENLABS_API_KEY", "TABPFN_TOKEN"):
            out += [f"alnum_only={v.isalnum()}", f"has_dash={'-' in v}", f"has_underscore={'_' in v}",
                    f"has_space={' ' in v}", f"sk-prefix={v.startswith('sk-')}"]
    except Exception as exc:
        out.append(f"inspect-error={type(exc).__name__}")
    return out


for n, raw in enumerate(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text().splitlines(), 1):
    line = raw.strip()
    if not line:
        print(f"{n:>3} (blank)")
        continue
    if line.startswith("#"):
        print(f"{n:>3} (comment)")
        continue
    flags = []
    if line.startswith("export "):
        flags.append("export")
        line = line[7:].lstrip()
    name, eq, value = line.partition("=")
    if not eq:
        print(f"{n:>3} (no '=')")
        continue
    if name != name.strip():
        flags.append("space-around-name")
    name = name.strip()
    if value != value.strip():
        flags.append("space-around-value")
    v = value.strip()
    q = v[:1] if v[:1] in ("'", '"') else ""
    if q:
        flags.append("double-quoted" if q == '"' else "single-quoted")
        if not (len(v) > 1 and v.endswith(q)):
            flags.append("UNCLOSED-QUOTE")
        v = v[1:-1] if len(v) > 1 and v.endswith(q) else v[1:]
    if " #" in value:
        flags.append("has-space-hash")
    flags.append(f"len={len(v)}" if v else "EMPTY")
    print(f"{n:>3} {name} " + " ".join(flags + (facts(name, v) if v else [])))

1	"""The Tinker auth endpoints `tinker auth login` and `tinker auth logout` use.
2	
3	- GET /api/v1/auth/apikey/me, which verifies the API key presented in the
4	  X-API-Key header and returns its public metadata. Login uses it to check the
5	  key the user pasted before storing it.
6	- DELETE /api/v1/auth/apikey/me, which deletes the API key presented in the
7	  X-API-Key header (and nothing else — it deliberately cannot delete other
8	  keys). Logout uses it to revoke the stored key it is about to discard.
9	
10	Neither authenticates with a resolved SDK credential — they run before one is
11	stored, or with only the raw key in hand — so they go over a plain httpx
12	client rather than the SDK client (which resolves a credential up front).
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	from typing import Optional, TypeVar
18	
19	import httpx
20	from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError
21	
22	# The base URL resolution is shared with the SDK client (see tinker.lib.base_url)
23	# so `tinker auth login` always talks to the same deployment the SDK will.
24	from tinker.lib.base_url import resolve_base_url
25	from tinker.lib.credentials import ApiKeyDetails
26	
27	_ModelT = TypeVar("_ModelT", bound=BaseModel)
28	
29	
30	class AuthApiError(Exception):
31	    """A call to the Tinker auth API failed."""
32	
33	
34	class SelfApiKeyResponse(BaseModel):
35	    """The response of the current API key endpoint."""
36	
37	    key_id: int
38	    name: str
39	    note: str
40	    details: ApiKeyDetails
41	
42	
43	class TinkerAuthApi:
44	    """Client for the Tinker API endpoints used to log in and out."""
45	
46	    def __init__(self, http_client: httpx.Client, *, base_url: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
47	        self._http = http_client
48	        self._base_url = resolve_base_url(base_url)
49	
50	    @property
51	    def base_url(self) -> str:
52	        return self._base_url
53	
54	    def get_self_api_key(self, api_key: str) -> SelfApiKeyResponse:
55	        """Verify `api_key` and return its public metadata."""
56	        response = self._request("GET", "/api/v1/auth/apikey/me", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
57	        return self._parse(response, SelfApiKeyResponse)
58	
59	    def delete_self_api_key(self, api_key: str) -> None:
60	        """Delete `api_key` itself on the server, revoking it everywhere."""
61	        self._request("DELETE", "/api/v1/auth/apikey/me", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
62	
63	    def _request(
64	        self, method: str, path: str, *, headers: Optional[dict[str, str]] = None
65	    ) -> httpx.Response:
66	        url = f"{self._base_url}/{path.lstrip('/')}"
67	        try:
68	            response = self._http.request(method, url, headers=headers)
69	        except httpx.HTTPError as e:
70	            raise AuthApiError(f"Could not reach the Tinker API at {self._base_url}: {e}") from e
71	        if not response.is_success:
72	            raise AuthApiError(f"{_detail(response)} (HTTP {response.status_code} from {path})")
73	        return response
74	
75	    @staticmethod
76	    def _parse(response: httpx.Response, model: type[_ModelT]) -> _ModelT:
77	        try:
78	            return model.model_validate(response.json())
79	        except (ValueError, ValidationError) as e:
80	            raise AuthApiError(f"The Tinker API returned an unexpected response: {e}") from e
81

"""config reads the environment first, then .env, and knows both Ultramarine key names."""

from paperghosts import config


def test_env_file_lines(tmp_path):
    env = tmp_path / ".env"
    env.write_text(
        "# a comment = with an equals sign\n"
        "\n"
        "PLAIN=abc\n"
        " SPACED = abc def \n"
        "URI=REDACTED"
        'DOUBLE="quoted value"\n'
        "SINGLE='quoted'\n"
        "EMPTY=\n"
        "no equals sign\n"
    )
    assert config.read_env_file(env) == {
        "PLAIN": "abc",
        "SPACED": "abc def",
        "URI": "REDACTED",
        "DOUBLE": "quoted value",
        "SINGLE": "quoted",
        "EMPTY": "",
    }
    assert config.read_env_file(tmp_path / "missing") == {}  # Render has no .env


def test_setting_reads_environment_then_env_file_then_alias(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    env = tmp_path / ".env"
    env.write_text("SERPAPI_API_KEY=from-file\nPAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY=from-file\nHF_TOKEN=\n")
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "ENV_FILE", env)
    for name in ("SERPAPI_API_KEY", "ULTRAMARINE_API_KEY", "PAPERINSTRUMENTS_API_KEY", "HF_TOKEN"):
        monkeypatch.delenv(name, raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setenv("SERPAPI_API_KEY", "from-env")

    assert config.setting("SERPAPI_API_KEY").get() == "from-env"
    assert config.setting("ULTRAMARINE_API_KEY").get() == "from-file"
    assert not config.setting("HF_TOKEN")

"""Sentry stays off without a DSN, and its events carry no query strings, coordinates,
local variables or host name."""

import random
import socket
import uuid

import pytest
import sentry_sdk
from sentry_sdk.client import NonRecordingClient

from paperghosts import config
from paperghosts.observability.sentry import init_sentry


@pytest.fixture
def clean_sentry(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "ENV_FILE", tmp_path / "missing")
    monkeypatch.delenv("SENTRY_DSN", raising=False)
    yield
    sentry_sdk.get_client().close()
    sentry_sdk.get_global_scope().set_client(None)


def test_off_without_a_dsn(clean_sentry):
    assert init_sentry("pipeline") is False
    assert isinstance(sentry_sdk.get_client(), NonRecordingClient)


def test_events_carry_no_query_strings_coordinates_locals_or_host(clean_sentry, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("SENTRY_DSN", "https://" + "0" * 32 + "@o1.ingest.us.sentry.io/1")
    assert init_sentry("pipeline") is True
    sent = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(sentry_sdk.get_client().transport, "capture_envelope", sent.append)
    # made at run time: Sentry ships source lines, so literals here would show up anyway
    key, lat, lon = uuid.uuid4().hex, random.uniform(25, 49), random.uniform(-124, -67)

    sentry_sdk.add_breadcrumb(
        category="httpx",
        data={"url": f"https://serpapi.com/search?api_key={key}", "http.query": f"api_key={key}"},
    )

    def near(lat, lon):
        uri = f"REDACTED"  # noqa: F841  a local that must not ship
        raise RuntimeError(f"no reports near /api/near?lat={lat}&lon={lon}")

    try:
        near(lat, lon)
    except RuntimeError:
        sentry_sdk.capture_exception()

    body = b"".join(envelope.serialize() for envelope in sent).decode()
    assert "no reports near /api/near" in body
    for private in (key, str(lat), str(lon), socket.gethostname()):
        assert private not in body

"""Sentry for the API and the pipeline: off without a DSN, and nothing personal or secret
leaves this machine."""

import re

import sentry_sdk

from paperghosts.config import setting

# a URL's query string, after scheme://host/path or a bare /path
QUERY = re.compile(r"((?:\w+:/)?/[^\s?#]*)\?[^\s#]*")
DROPPED_KEYS = {
    "query_string",
    "http.query",
    "lat",
    "lon",
    "lng",
    "latitude",
    "longitude",
    "coordinates",
}


def scrub(value):
    """Strips query strings and coordinate fields anywhere in an event."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return QUERY.sub(r"\1", value)
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: scrub(v) for k, v in value.items() if str(k).lower() not in DROPPED_KEYS}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [scrub(v) for v in value]
    return value


def init_sentry(component: str) -> bool:
    """Starts Sentry for "api" or "pipeline". Without SENTRY_DSN it does nothing."""
    dsn = setting("SENTRY_DSN")
    if not dsn:
        return False
    sentry_sdk.init(
        dsn=dsn.get(),
        environment=component,  # the API and the pipeline share one project
        server_name=component,  # the default is the host name, which can name its owner
        send_default_pii=False,
        include_local_variables=False,  # locals can hold keys, URIs and coordinates
        traces_sample_rate=1.0,
        before_send=lambda event, hint: scrub(event),
        before_send_transaction=lambda event, hint: scrub(event),
    )
    return True

def _resolve_data_collection(options: "Dict[str, Any]") -> "DataCollection":
    """
    Resolve the effective ``DataCollection`` dict from client ``options``.

    Reads ``data_collection``, ``send_default_pii``, ``include_local_variables``
    and ``include_source_context`` and returns a fully-resolved dict with
    concrete values for every field.

    ``data_collection`` must be a plain ``dict``.

    Must be called exactly once per options dict, before ``client._get_options``
    overwrites ``options["data_collection"]`` with the resolved result. Feeding an
    already-resolved dict back in would flip ``provided_by_user`` to ``True``.
    """
    user_dc = options.get("data_collection")
    if user_dc is None:
        user_dc = options.get("_experiments", {}).get("data_collection")

    send_default_pii = options.get("send_default_pii")

    include_local_variables = (
        bool(options.get("include_local_variables"))
        if options.get("include_local_variables") is not None
        else True
    )
    include_source_context = (
        bool(options.get("include_source_context"))
        if options.get("include_source_context") is not None
        else True
    )

    if user_dc is not None:
        if not isinstance(user_dc, dict):
            raise TypeError(
                "`data_collection` must be a dict, got {!r}.".format(
                    type(user_dc).__name__
                )
            )
        if send_default_pii is not None:
            warnings.warn(
                "`send_default_pii` is deprecated and ignored when "
                "`data_collection` is set.",
                DeprecationWarning,
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        return _resolve_explicit(
            user_dc,
        )

    return _map_from_send_default_pii(
        send_default_pii=bool(send_default_pii),
        include_local_variables=include_local_variables,
        include_source_context=include_source_context,
    )

"""make smoke: one workflow whose activity heartbeats, fails once on purpose and recovers
through its retry policy. Needs `make temporal` and `make worker` running."""

import asyncio
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

from temporalio import activity, workflow
from temporalio.client import Client
from temporalio.common import RetryPolicy
from temporalio.exceptions import ApplicationError

from paperghosts.workflows import TASK_QUEUE, TEMPORAL


@activity.defn
async def count_steps(steps: int) -> dict:
    info = activity.info()
    # a retry resumes after the last step its failed attempt heartbeated
    done = info.heartbeat_details[0] if info.heartbeat_details else 0
    for step in range(done + 1, steps + 1):
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        activity.heartbeat(step)
        if info.attempt == 1 and step == steps // 2:
            raise ApplicationError(f"injected failure at step {step}")
    return {"attempt": info.attempt, "resumed_after": done}


@workflow.defn
class SmokeWorkflow:
    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, steps: int) -> dict:
        return await workflow.execute_activity(
            count_steps,
            steps,
            start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=30),
            heartbeat_timeout=timedelta(seconds=5),
            retry_policy=RetryPolicy(initial_interval=timedelta(seconds=1), maximum_attempts=3),
        )


async def main():
    client = await Client.connect(TEMPORAL)
    workflow_id = "smoke-" + datetime.now(UTC).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    result = await client.execute_workflow(
        SmokeWorkflow.run,
        6,
        id=workflow_id,
        task_queue=TASK_QUEUE,
        execution_timeout=timedelta(seconds=60),
    )
    print(f"workflow {workflow_id}: {result}")
    print(f"history: http://localhost:8233/namespaces/default/workflows/{workflow_id}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

"""make worker: runs the workflows and activities against the local Temporal dev server."""

import asyncio

from temporalio.client import Client
from temporalio.worker import Worker

from paperghosts.observability.sentry import init_sentry
from paperghosts.workflows import TASK_QUEUE, TEMPORAL
from paperghosts.workflows.smoke import SmokeWorkflow, count_steps


async def main():
    init_sentry("pipeline")
    client = await Client.connect(TEMPORAL)
    worker = Worker(
        client, task_queue=TASK_QUEUE, workflows=[SmokeWorkflow], activities=[count_steps]
    )
    print(f"worker polling task queue {TASK_QUEUE!r} on {TEMPORAL}")
    await worker.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

**15. Sentry collects nothing about people, and nothing a local variable holds.**
- sentry-sdk 2.73 deprecates `send_default_pii`, so `init_sentry` sets `data_collection` instead. """IIIF crops of article clippings from the Library of Congress page scans."""

import re

IIIF = "https://tile.loc.gov/image-services/iiif"
BATCH_PATH = re.compile(
    r"/data/batches/(?P<batch>[^/]+)/data/(?P<lccn>[^/]+)/(?P<reel>[^/]+)"
    r"/(?P<issue>[^/]+)/(?P<seq>[^/.]+)\.jp2$"
)


def service_id(raw_data_loc: str) -> str:
    """The page's IIIF service, from the batch path AmericanStories records for its scan."""
    path = BATCH_PATH.search(raw_data_loc)
    if path is None:
        raise ValueError("raw_data_loc is not a Chronicling America batch path")
    awardee = path["batch"].split("_")[0]
    return (
        f"service:ndnp:{awardee}:batch_{path['batch']}:data:"
        f"{path['lccn']}:{path['reel']}:{path['issue']}:{path['seq']}"
    )


def crop_url(service: str, boxes: list[dict]) -> str:
    """One crop covering every box, in the scan's own pixels, at half size."""
    x0, y0 = min(b["x0"] for b in boxes), min(b["y0"] for b in boxes)
    x1, y1 = max(b["x1"] for b in boxes), max(b["y1"] for b in boxes)
    return f"{IIIF}/{service}/{x0},{y0},{x1 - x0},{y1 - y0}/pct:50/0/default.jpg"

"""The API answers in the SRS contract's shapes: health with Atlas up or down, a skeleton
article, and the error format for an article that doesn't exist."""

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from api.main import app


class FakeAtlas:
    """Stands in for the paperghosts database: a ping, and one skeleton article."""

    def __init__(self, reachable=True):
        self.skeleton, self.reachable = self, reachable

    async def command(self, name):
        if not self.reachable:
            raise ConnectionError("no route to Atlas")
        return {"ok": 1}

    async def find_one(self, query):
        return {"_id": "a1", "text": "Knockings."} if query == {"_id": "a1"} else None


def test_health_skeleton_and_not_found():
    client = TestClient(app)  # not entered, so the lifespan never reaches Atlas or Sentry
    app.state.db = FakeAtlas()

    health = client.get("/api/health").json()
    assert (health["ok"], health["atlas"]) == (True, True) and health["version"]
    assert client.get("/api/skeleton/a1").json() == {"_id": "a1", "text": "Knockings."}
    missing = client.get("/api/skeleton/a2")
    assert missing.status_code == 404
    assert missing.json()["error"]["code"] == "not_found" and missing.json()["error"]["message"]

"""make api: the read-only API over MongoDB Atlas. Phase 1 serves the walking skeleton."""

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from importlib.metadata import version

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from pymongo import AsyncMongoClient

from paperghosts.config import setting
from paperghosts.observability.sentry import init_sentry


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app):
    init_sentry("api")
    client = AsyncMongoClient(setting("MONGODB_URI").get(), serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5_000)
    app.state.db = client["paperghosts"]
    yield
    await client.close()


app = FastAPI(title="Paper Ghosts", lifespan=lifespan)


@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    try:
        await app.state.db.command("ping")
        atlas = True
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001  any failure means Atlas can't be reached from here
        atlas = False
    return {"ok": True, "atlas": atlas, "version": version("paperghosts")}


@app.get("/api/skeleton/{article_id}")
async def skeleton(article_id: str):
    article = await app.state.db.skeleton.find_one({"_id": article_id})
    if article is None:
        error = {"code": "not_found", "message": "No skeleton article has that id."}
        return JSONResponse({"error": error}, status_code=404)
    return article

"""Loads the walking skeleton's article into the scratch collection paperghosts.skeleton.

Run after scripts/phase1_env.py, which saves the 1850 Stratford matches to data/skeleton/.
"""

import re
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
import orjson
import pymongo

from paperghosts.config import setting
from paperghosts.ingest.crops import crop_url, service_id

MATCHES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "data" / "skeleton" / "stratford_1850.json"
PAPER, DATE = "Lewistown gazette", "1850-07-26"


def page_service(match):
    raw_data_loc = match["page"]["scan"].get("raw_data_loc")
    if raw_data_loc:
        return service_id(raw_data_loc)
    # some scans have no raw_data_loc, so ask loc.gov which batch holds the page
    name = match["member"].rsplit("/", 1)[-1].removesuffix(".json")
    date, _, lccn, reel, issue, seq = name.split("_")
    item = f"https://www.loc.gov/item/{lccn}/{date}/ed-{int(issue[-2:])}/"
    listing = httpx.get(item, params={"fo": "json"}, timeout=30, follow_redirects=True).text
    found = re.search(rf"service:ndnp:[a-z]+:batch_\w+?:data:{lccn}:{reel}:{issue}:{seq}", listing)
    if found is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"loc.gov lists no IIIF service for {name}")
    return found[0]


def main():
    match = next(
        m
        for m in orjson.loads(MATCHES.read_bytes())
        if m["page"]["lccn"]["title"].startswith(PAPER) and m["page"]["edition"]["date"] == DATE
    )
    article, page = match["article"], match["page"]
    document = {
        "_id": article["id"],
        "paper": page["lccn"]["title"],
        "date": page["edition"]["date"],
        "headline": article["headline"],
        "text": article["article"],
        "bbox_list": article["bbox_list"],
        "crop_url": crop_url(page_service(match), article["bbox_list"]),
    }
    with pymongo.MongoClient(setting("MONGODB_URI").get(), serverSelectionTimeoutMS=10_000) as client:
        client["paperghosts"]["skeleton"].replace_one({"_id": document["_id"]}, document, upsert=True)
    print(f"loaded {document['_id']}")
    print(f"crop {document['crop_url']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
